title: Balance the volume
rule: If one half is roomy, keep the other half clean.
body: A relaxed knit over slim jeans, or a neat tee over wide trousers. One loose half and one fitted half reads as deliberate. Two loose halves can swamp the frame.

title: Wide legs need a shoe with weight
rule: A slim shoe gets swallowed by the extra fabric. Go chunkier.
body: Wide and baggy trousers pool around the foot. A chunky sneaker, a skate shoe or a boot holds its own against that volume, so the outfit stays balanced from top to bottom.

title: Slim legs, sleek shoes
rule: A narrow trouser wants a low, clean shoe.
body: Loafers, minimal leather sneakers and Chelsea boots follow the line of a slim or straight leg. A very chunky sole at the end of a skinny leg looks heavy.

title: Neutrals go with everything
rule: Black, white, grey, navy, cream and beige never fight.
body: Build most outfits on neutrals and nothing competes, so the shapes do the talking. It's the easiest way to make a wardrobe where everything pairs with everything.

title: One bold color at a time
rule: Let one piece be loud and keep the rest quiet.
body: A green hoodie or a red knit looks confident on a neutral base. Two strong colors at once start to argue. Pick the one you love most today and let it lead.

title: Earth tones get along
rule: Olive, brown, rust and tan sit naturally with denim, cream and white.
body: Earthy colors share a warmth, so they pair with each other and with the softer neutrals. Olive with cream, brown with denim: it looks considered without trying.

title: One pattern per outfit
rule: Two patterns compete. Keep one and make the rest plain.
body: A striped shirt with plain trousers is easy on the eye. Stripes with checks need real skill to pull off. When in doubt, one pattern and solids around it.

title: Denim on denim: contrast the washes
rule: Two denims work when one is clearly lighter than the other.
body: A light jacket over dark jeans looks intentional. Two pieces in nearly the same wash read like an accidental suit. Make the difference obvious.

title: Brown and black: let one be the accent
rule: Brown and black at the same weight fight. Keep one small.
body: A brown knit with black trousers splits the outfit in two. Brown loafers with black jeans work, because the shoes are a small accent. Or swap the black for navy or cream.

title: Big on big, on purpose
rule: Oversized top and baggy trousers only work with a strong signal.
body: Give it a reason: a chunky shoe or a boxy, cropped top. Without one, all that fabric looks like the clothes are wearing you.
